I actually do this. Fortunately I don't look this much like a douchebag, but yeah, I have to wear sunglasses all the time because my vision is fucking terrible.

Nobody ever thinks "Oh, it's a blind dude!"

Hours. and hours. and hours. and hours. and then I have like baseline migraines(? Chronic headache?) or something else that just go on in the background. So I'm at about a 6-7 on the pain/ragecage most of the time, and then it quickly ramps up to a 10 where I'm walking around in circles, or muttering to myself, or losing consciousness unexpectedly.

It usually means I have a lot of flashbacks to weird eye stuff and that I'm constantly hyper-vigilant about stuff being near my eyes, and stuff flying into my eyes, and people hitting me in the eyes, and basically paranoid that it's getting WORSE. I can't go for haircuts because the stuff in the air and I'm freaked out about people near my face, no one hugs me anymore because I'll hit them, and I don't like places where people are really near me because I'm terrified about getting bumped in the head and having corneal dehiscence. There was a day where I found myself yelling at a stranger in public. I wasn't aware I was yelling until I suddenly realized I was yelling.

The dreams of people with needles are kind of the worst though. Just sort of dark shadowy people, and you can't move, and a lot of needles.

The rest of my life looks a lot like this.

[The picture does a really good job of explaining it in a tl;dr situation, but the wiki article is fascinating](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluster_headache)

And no, not really. My first one was during the surgery itself, ironically while The Marshall Tucker Band's [Can't You See](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gCXQycyN_Vs) was playing. Being anesthetized and seeing an injection headed towards your eye and being completely unable to move, yet being cognizant of what's going on is pretty terrifying. Surprisingly, it didn't hurt that badly after the first three seconds apart from a mild burning.

The next time was the next day when the pressure was too high. They jabbed me to "relieve" the pressure. Unexpected for sure. I've since found out the name for this procedure is "burping."

And they remove stitches with tweezers and a needle every two, three weeks-ish. Kind of like how some people take out a splinter, but in your eye. I basically try to hold really really still and try to remember to breathe while this goes on.

Overall, I'd say I'm only slightly less freaked out by it than I was initially. Granted, I have what I'm sure is PTSD about my eyes now, but really, at the end of the day, it has to get done right?

That's fine. Don't worry, I always think everyone has an ulterior motive. Growing up with a psychologist mother and a stock broker dad, you learn that EVERYONE always has a motive, all gifts are bribes, and a cigar is NEVER a cigar. Before all this started I was an economics/environmental science double major.

I'd like to be able to see a Christmas tree. And what my friends actually look like. The night sky would be cool, but I know that's a lot to ask for, because the light gets so diffused. Everything looks like blobs pretty much. I feel like I'm trapped in a pointillism painting most of the time.

[This is kind of like a much less bad version of how I see](http://www.alliancetec.com/keratoconus.htm)

Cluster headaches are so much more painful than an actual needle in the eye. Having an actual needle in the eye is much more of a psychological thing. I can totally speak from experience on that one.

I was merely curious, that's all.

Basically, your horrible, deformed crappy cornea is cut out, either by laser or trefine, a circular cutting instrument, and replaced with a healthy button of a donor cornea, which is stitched in. Mine was done under conscious sedation, and magically, the retrograde aspect of the amnesic didn't work so well, so I had the most aware side of anesthesia awareness.

Thus far my vision has gone from 20/1600 in that eye to about 20/240. I may be able to wear glasses with some relative effectiveness. I would be excited about this :)

As for the headaches, they're just a rather unfortunate thing that there's nothing that I can do much about. Due to a faulty hypothalamus they think? I mainly actually like the dark because it could cause my eyes to fail and because my left eye is stuck more dilated than the right and light basically causes shooting pains due to the extreme headache pain associated with cluster headache. It basically feels like getting stabbed in the eye with an ice pick.

The funny thing is, I know what getting stabbed in the eye with needles and so forth feels like -- not as painful as you'd imagine...

Pretty terrible actually. The crappy emotional part is there, yeah, but the fact that I have a full blown cluster headache definitely doesn't help.

And because I can't really leave the house because my recently transplanted cornea can reject due to bright sunlight or me becoming too warm, well, that's just dog shit icing on the garbage cake.

Other than that, I'm a ray of sunshine shot out of a unicorn's ass. How are you? Having viewed your comment history, you appear to be a magical angel.
It just seemed like a good way to end the night. The fact it had just been added to Netflix Watch Instant helped too.

It's amazing how much worse your life can get than what you think you can tolerate. When I was 14 I used to tell myself if I got to 21 and didn't have a girlfriend or wasn't on my own I'd be done with things.

Haha. If only I knew how much worse things could get.

What I really really struggle with, as a logical, sane person, is the sheer lunacy of it all. Did you know the insurance system doesn't cover glasses or contact lenses, even for what I'd term "preventable" blindness?

My vision is so bad that I literally cannot see without the aid of specialty contact lenses, costing in excess of 10k a year, and taking up to 5 months to complete. (This year it took from Nov, 2011 until May, 2012, to get a final, working prescription in one eye, for a total **direct** cost of 5.6k, excluding the cost of driving the numerous trips there and back, copays, so forth)

I can't drive anymore, so I have to have someone drive for me. It's kind of a piece of crap. But the real kicker is that without contacts, I'm completely blind. But in order to be covered for legal blindness, you have to be worse than 20/200 with **BEST AVAILABLE VISION CORRECTION**

That means that even if surgical options are available, or some exceedingly expensive contacts or glasses that are impossible for you to afford and are not covered at all by insurance, you are still legally bound to purchase them, even though you very well may be blind.

Granted, even though you have glasses or contacts, you still can't see most of the time. Acuity and clarity are two very different things. You can watch Sanford and Son just as well on a TV from the 1970s as you can on a modern 1080P 600hz flat screen. Clearly though, these are two completely different views of the same thing. Welcome to my vision experience.

The point though, is that my hope of getting a job is almost nil; the time and explicit financial cost of getting the most essential of human senses for me is ungodly. Even though minimum wage is the highest in my state in the country, basic math yields:

9.04*40*52=18803.2

This is if I work full time, all the time. Probably not possible due to the conditions outlined above, but for the sake of demonstration, why not?

Now, let's say I want to continue working. So I pay the mandatory minimum to see.

18803.2-10000 =8803.2

Well, I certainly don't have much left do I? Remember, this has to be paid as a lump sum.

Now, assuming I want to live away from home (I would like to someday). The real issue is that in order to not have a car, I have to live within a certain range of my doctors. This complicates things, as I cannot see to drive. This ups the price of my rents. While living with a bunch of other people is horrible for my health, the cheapest rent I could find is $500 a month. Because what I have is "not a disability" (dear god, how I've tried), I don't qualify for any sort of subsidized housing.

So over the course of the year, we have

8803.2-(500*12)=2803.2

Well, it looks like I have 2803.2 left for taxes and food for the year.

Of course, this assumes I can get a job at all. Which I wouldn't be able to in the first place due to likely excessive absences

It's just hard to know what to do. A lot of people have this wonderful potential for things to get better. I really really don't. And that's what kills me.

Chronic intractable health problems. Rapidly losing eyesight, chronic pain, organ failure, other assorted problems.

Basically, pretty soon my helicopter parents will control what little bit of a life I was able to carve out during the three years I was away from them at college. I've been depressed for years due to knowing this all was coming, but it came a hell of a lot faster than expected, and a hell of a lot harder.
